elements.element: Customer owns deliverables/work product created for it
elements.evidence: 14.2 "Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer."
"Vendor hereby irrevocably assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in each Deliverable."

elements.element: Perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to Vendor IP embedded in deliverables
elements.evidence: 13.2 "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use ... modify ..."; 14.3 "To the extent Vendor Technology is incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable, the perpetual licence in Section 13.2 applies."

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data
elements.evidence: 14.1 "Customer owns all Customer Data ... No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process"
14.4 "No jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument"

elements.element: Vendor owns generic tools and know-how
elements.evidence: 14.3 "Vendor retains Vendor Technology"; Deliverables "exclude Vendor Technology and generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how"

elements.element: Perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense Deliverables
elements.evidence: 13.2 grants the perpetual licence only for "software and Vendor Technology ... embedded in a Deliverable" and permits only "permit contractors to support that material" — no sublicensing right, and no perpetual licence to Deliverables as such; 14.2 still gives only a "revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term."

reasons: The two operations vest Deliverable ownership in Customer and add an express Vendor assignment, so every preferred atomic element (ownership, assignment, Vendor pre-existing IP retention, perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free embedded-IP licence via 13.2/14.3, Customer Data rights in 14.1, no joint ownership in 14.4) is present.
Minimality is satisfied: only the ownership operator in 14.2's first sentence was changed and one concise assignment sentence added; no unrelated sentence or other-level requirement was imported.

Intent is not preserved: the untouched second sentence of 14.2 — "Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term" — now contradicts Customer's ownership and assignment, leaving a dangling mechanic under which Vendor could purport to revoke or time-limit Customer's use of its own Deliverables.

Fix: delete or replace that residual licence sentence (e.g. strike it, or recast as "Vendor receives no licence to Deliverables except as needed to perform the Services") so ownership is not undercut.
Fallback is separately incomplete (no sublicensing right and Deliverable licence still revocable/term-limited), but that is irrelevant because the drafter's locked target is preferred.
